diseases.name: Infectious Coryza
diseases.description: Acute bacterial respiratory disease caused by Avibacterium paragallinarum

care_recommendations.title: Antimicrobial Treatment
care_recommendations.detail: Early stages can be managed with antibiotics (such as erythromycin, oxytetracycline, or sulfonamides) prescribed by a veterinarian.

care_recommendations.title: Isolation and Biosecurity
care_recommendations.detail: Isolate sick birds immediately, practice an 'all-in, all-out' flock management system, and thoroughly clean and disinfect coops.

diseases.name: Fowl Pox
diseases.description: Viral disease caused by Avipoxvirus causing dry cutaneous lesions on unfeathered facial skin and eyelids

care_recommendations.title: No Direct Cure
care_recommendations.detail: There is no specific antiviral treatment for fowl pox. The dry cutaneous form usually resolves naturally in 2 to 4 weeks.

care_recommendations.title: Supportive Care
care_recommendations.detail: Isolate sick birds, keep the coop clean, provide easy access to feed and water, and apply mild antiseptics or iodine on dry skin lesions. Broad-spectrum antibiotics may treat secondary bacterial infections. Do not pick at scabs to prevent spreading the virus.

care_recommendations.title: Prevention
care_recommendations.detail: Vaccinate the flock using live attenuated fowl pox or pigeon pox vaccines (administered via wing-web puncture) and strictly control mosquito populations around the coop.

diseases.name: Healthy Eye
diseases.description: No ocular disease detected - eyes appear bright, alert, and clear with normal peri-orbital skin

care_recommendations.title: Flock Maintenance
care_recommendations.detail: Maintain regular biosecurity, clean watering stations daily, and conduct routine ocular inspections every 7 days.

diseases.name: Healthy Wing
diseases.description: No postural or wing paralysis detected - wings held tight, symmetrical, and alert against the flank

care_recommendations.title: Optimal Fitness
care_recommendations.detail: Continue scheduled exercise and routine physical conditioning. Verify roosting bars are clean and free of rough edges.

diseases.name: Newcastle Disease
diseases.description: Highly contagious viral disease caused by Avian Paramyxovirus Serotype 1 attacking the nervous system and causing wing drooping

care_recommendations.title: Strict Isolation
care_recommendations.detail: Move affected gamefowl immediately to a completely separate quarantine pen far away from healthy birds. NDV spreads rapidly through the air and dander from flapping wings.

care_recommendations.title: Sanitize and Clean Housing
care_recommendations.detail: Wash down cages, feeders, and waterers with a reliable disinfectant (such as Virkon, bleach solution, or iodine-based cleaners).

care_recommendations.title: Supportive Care
care_recommendations.detail: Provide clean water mixed with electrolytes and water-soluble Vitamin B-complex for nervous system support. Place feed and water directly in front of the bird's breast so it does not have to walk.

care_recommendations.title: Culling and Safe Disposal
care_recommendations.detail: If gamefowl is severely paralyzed or dying, cull the bird humanely. Never throw carcasses in rivers or open bins. Burn or bury deep in the ground (at least 3 feet down) away from water sources, coated with quicklime (apog).

care_recommendations.title: Emergency Vaccination
care_recommendations.detail: Immediately vaccinate all other healthy, asymptomatic gamefowl in your yard using a live NDV vaccine (such as LaSota strain) to boost immunity before exposure.
